A finite subset has gcd one: choose a finite-subset gcd of least positive value and adjoin any return time that would lower it. Fix a∈R_x. The residues of the additive semigroup generated by that finite subset form a subgroup of the finite cyclic group Z/aZ; gcd one makes it the whole group. Choose a realized representative in each of finitely many residues, then add enough copies of a to obtain every sufficiently large integer. For u→v in r steps, append a sufficiently long loop at v. The proof is finite arithmetic, not a renewal theorem or a choice argument.
